summary: Members supported a possible moratorium on vape shops while the Zoning Commission considers it. They also agreed to send a letter to Public Works supporting city ownership of a freight rail line. Year-end budget carryovers and transfers were approved.

ECONOMIC AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT 
Thursday, August 6, 2026 at 5:00pm 
City Council Chambers, City Hall, 111 N. Main Street & on Zoom 
 
 
Present:  Mayor Zoppo-Sassu -- Chair, City Council Member Susan Tyler, and 
Commissioners Dave Mills, Tom Hick (Zoom), Jason Paul Sirko, 
Commissioners LaQuita Kearney-Gonzalez (Zoom), Marvin (Mickey) 
Goldwasser, and Louise Provenzano 
 
Absent:  Howard Schmelder, Vice Chair 
 
ECD Staff:  Justin Malley - Executive Director, Dr. Dawn Leger - Grants Administrator 
 
Guests: Julien Garcia, Sei Bella Restaurant, 182 Main St., Bristol 
 
I. Call to Order 
Mayor Zoppo-Sassu called the meeting to order at 5:00pm and led all present in 
the Pledge of Allegiance.  
 
II. Public Participation 
There was no Public Participation. 
 
III. Approval of Minutes 
A. Minutes of the July 2, 2026 Regular Meeting 
The mayor called for a motion to approve the Minutes of the July 2, 2026 Regular 
Meeting. Commissioner Mills made the motion to accept the Minutes. The 
motion was seconded by City Council Member Tyler. No edits were noted. All 
were in favor and the Minutes were accepted into the record. Commissioners 
Provenzano and Goldwasser abstained from the vote. 
 
IV.         Consent Agenda 
A.  Communications 
B.  Economic Development/Grants/Marketing Report 
The mayor called for a motion to accept the Consent Agenda. Commissioner 
Goldwasser made the motion to accept, and the motion was seconded by 
Commissioner Mills. There was no discussion. All were in favor and the Consent 
Agenda was accepted into the record.
V.         New Business 
A.  Industrial Update 
Justin Malley advised there was no Industrial Update at this time. The Industrial 
Committee does expect to meet next month to consider site plan approval for 
Integrity Manufacturing, Lot #6 of the Southeast Bristol Business Park (SEBBP). 
 
B. Downtown Update 
Julien Garcia of Sei Bella Restaurant introduced himself and his project at 182 
Main Street. He is a restaurant developer and was drawn to Bristol after seeing 
the city’s development over the past few years. Sei Bella (Italian for “Hey, 
Beautiful”) is an Italian restaurant with a freestyle and seasonal menu planned 
in the space formerly home to Pint & Plate.  
 
Sei Bella’s décor is modern, with an emphasis on celebrating women. Mr. Garcia 
is using various forms and styles of art which he feels is especially important 
because the restaurant is located in the Art & Culture District. His goal is to 
create a welcoming date night venue that is also a destination restaurant 
drawing out of town visitors to Bristol. 
 
Discussion followed, including the inclusion of homemade pastas on the menu 
and the restaurant’s approach to the bar and cocktail offerings. The goal is for 
every patron to leave feeling energized by the ambiance and the culture. An 
opening is planned for late summer/early fall. 
 
Justin Malley spoke to the Downtown parking video that the ECD Department 
has commissioned. The goal of the video is to further educate the community 
about their parking options when visiting downtown. Businesses such as 
Tavello, Mr. P’s, Wheeler Health and others are included in the video. It was 
noted that Wheeler Health’s parking lot is available for public parking on nights 
and weekends, and that includes the Hope Street Parking garage. The parking 
video will be shared across social media and the city website when it is 
completed. 
 
The New England Auto Museum is holding their car show on Hope Street this 
weekend from 3pm to 8pm. This is an example of how the newly developed 
space is welcoming community events.
Apex Golf is a Bristol family start-up opening in the former Biker’s Edge space at 
99 Main Street. They will be a membership driven location for serious golf 
players and those learning the sport. Plans include an indoor putting green. 
 
Axis Barbershop, another new business in Centre Square, expects to open in a 
month. Next door to them is Cyriously Hair, a new high-end hair salon. Agave 
Azul is in the former Monterey Restaurant space on Riverside Avenue, and 
they’re looking at a soft opening on August 14th.  
 
C. Fiscal Year End Carryovers and Transfers 
The Carryovers and Transfers are a yearly line item at the close of the fiscal year.

• $1,153.24 from 1044101-581120-G2026 Conferences & Memberships

discussion. All were in favor and the Carryover Request was approved.

discussion. All were in favor and the Transfer Request was approved. 
 
D. ECD Policy Discussion 
The Board of Public Works referred to the ECD Board about a small piece of 
freight rail line that runs through the city. The city is currently responsible for 
maintaining this stretch of the rail from near the Plymouth town line to the area 
that used to be Firestone and New Departure (780 James P. Casey Road). 
 
The initial question from The Board of Public Works was about the possibility of 
the rail ownership moving to the private sector, but that may bring challenges 
better managed by the city. The mayor chairs the Public Works Board. She 
reported the discussion on this item at their meeting was engaging. That Board 
wanted the input of the ECD Board as use of the rail relates to economic 
development functions.  
 
Discussion followed, including liability, current maintenance frequency, and 
costs, which are typically $25,000 to $40,000 a year. These costs don’t include 
one-off issues like derailments or damage. The estimated cost over the past 20 
years is $2 million dollars.  
 
Based on the discussion, it was agreed that Justin Malley and the mayor will send 
a letter to Public Works recognizing the value of this freight line as a component
of transportation for the advancement of business goals. They will support the 
city retaining ownership of the freight line. 
 
Justin Malley noted that new State legislation passed regarding ways 
communities can work with and/or handle vape shops. The Zoning Commission 
has been asked to consider a moratorium on allowing additional vape shops to 
open in the city. The goal would be to allow time to better understand the options 
this legislation provides. The Commission reached out to this Board for their 
input on this item. 
 
They mayor shared that a new City Ordinance regarding vape shop licensing had 
also been passed to go into effect on October 1, 2026. The main concerns with 
the vape shops are resident’s health and safety, impact on other local 
businesses, and compliance such as labelling and products offered.  
 
A recent step-up in enforcement identified problematic, non-compliant 
locations. The mayor noted that one part of the new State legislation is a daily 
$10,000 fine to landlords and/or building owners of those businesses found to be 
in violation. This is an example of the information the city needs time to 
understand and share out. 
 
Discussion followed, including how the moratorium would better set 
expectations for all parties going forward, clarify what the laws are, and ensure 
that the related City Ordinance is appropriate. The next Zoning Commission 
meeting is Monday, August 10th. The letter from the ECD Board would focus 
solely on the approving moratorium, especially to educate the city and the 
landlords. 
 
Following the discussion, the ECD Board clarified their support for the 
moratorium on the vape shops to allow the city time to best understand what 
actions it is afforded under the new State legislation, as well as time to advise 
shop landlords, tenants, neighbors and interested organizations from a public 
health and safety standpoint.  
 
City Council Member Tyler then made the following motion: 
 
Motion that this Board send a letter to the Zoning Commission to show our 
support for a moratorium with the vape shops.
The motion was seconded by Commissioner Gonzales. There was no further 
discussion. All were in favor and the motion was accepted into the record. 
 
VI.       New Business by Commissioners 
     There was no New Business by Commissioners. 
 
VII.     Old Business by Commissioners 
Commissioner Goldwasser asked about the Chippanee Golf Course. The mayor 
advised that they’re currently in price negotiations. She is scheduling an 
Executive Session with City Council for Wednesday, August 12th to provide 
updates, but no information is ready for public release or review at this time. 
 
VIII.    Committee Reports 
A. City Council Member Report 
City Council Member Tyler expressed thanks for the support and work done to 
promote the Little League Tournament. There’s been a lot of positive feedback 
from businesses regarding the Welcome banner and the signs for their windows. 
ECD Interns Kaidyn Sigmund and Colin Cavallari were instrumental in both of 
those initiatives. Discussion about the placement of additional signs by 
businesses followed with a note that signs shouldn’t block sight lines or create 
visual concerns. 
 
City businesses have asked about a survey with the goal of raising awareness of 
the business’ challenges, issues, and concerns. The mayor noted that the city’s 
Plan of Conservation and Development Update which includes a community 
engagement piece, is starting. It could allow for businesses to include their input. 
Discussion followed. 
 
Businesses also expressed concerns regarding the negative impact of code 
enforcement violations on their locations. Discussion followed with residents 
and businesses encouraged to contact the city when they notice violations. 
 
IX.     Adjournment 
With no further discussion, the mayor called for a motion to adjourn. The motion 
was made by Commissioner Provenzano and was seconded by Commissioner 
Goldwasser. All were in favor and the meeting adjourned at 6:15pm
Respectfully submitted, 
 
Sharon Arsego 
Recording Secretary
